newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LA Retail buys Skye for 115.6 mln rand.
newsitem.headline: LA Retail buys Skye for 115.6 mln rand.

text.p: South Africa's LA Retail Stores Ltd said on Wednesday it had bought branded clothing and footwear marketer Skye Products for 115.6 million rand.

The group said the deal would be financed by placing four million ordinary shares at 425 cents a share with management and 24.6 million "N" shares at 400 cents each with institutional investors, the existing management team of Skye and business associates of LA Retail.
It would be based on profit warranties of a pre-tax profit of not less than 22 million rand in the period to February 28, 1998.
LA Retail chief executive Abdul Peer told a media briefing "virtually all" institutional investors and several black empowerment groups had taken up the offer.
The group issued a cautionary on March 20 that it was engaged in talks that could affect its share price.
The deal, effective from March 1, is expected to boost LA's earnings to 27.5 cents a share from 19.2 cents and its net asset value per share to 83.8 cents from 52.6 cents.

Skye Products is the only South African licence holder of international clothing brands such as Converse, Saucony and Dickie and supplies more than 3,000 independent retailers as well as major chain stores. It also distributes Mille, Jump and Brentwood footwear.
Its turnover for the financial year to February 28 was 110 million rand with pre-tax profits of 17.5 million rand.
Peer said the two business would retain their separate identities and management teams and that LA Retail's Samson brand would be moved to the branding division of Skye within the next few weeks.
